sources.entry: AB Method by Ayoub Bensalah - A principled, spec-driven workflow that transforms large problems into focused, incremental missions using Claude Code's specialized sub agents. Includes slash-commands, sub agents, and specialized workflows designed for specific parts of the SDLC.

summary.one_liner: A spec-driven workflow system for Claude Code and Codex that grills a problem into a domain-grounded plan and then runs it as test-driven missions, or as an autonomous /goal loop.
summary.what_it_does: The installer (npx ab-method) detects .claude/ and/or .agents/ and installs slash commands and skills for Claude Code, Codex, or both, plus .ab-method/ workflow definitions, docs/ scaffolding, an AGENTS.md for Codex, and optional subagents. Every task and goal begins with a grill-with-docs step that checks terms against UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md and CONTEXT.md and records decisions as ADRs. Tasks are split into test-driven missions that the user reviews one at a time, or run autonomously with one subagent and one commit per mission. Goals are single objectives with a checkable stop condition, and roadmaps split a larger idea into a dependency-ordered graph of tasks. The README also describes critic steps (critique-plan, review-implementation, sync-architecture), a change-map that predicts touched modules, and a check-docs command that enforces word budgets on docs. It is also available as a plugin, which does not copy files into the project.
use_cases: Break a large feature into test-driven missions reviewed one at a time
Run a multi-step coding task autonomously with a verifiable stop condition
Plan a bigger project as an ordered set of tasks
Add tests to existing code not written test-first
Document a codebase's domain, tech stack and architecture for AI agents
Keep architecture and domain docs small and current
notable: Spec-driven flow: grill the problem first, then plan, then code, with ADRs recorded along the way
Choice of running a task interactively mission by mission, or as an autonomous /goal loop
Critic steps check the plan against the domain model before coding and the diff and docs after
Works with both Claude Code and Codex, installed via npx or as a plugin
Includes a /ab-cleanup migration path from 3.x to 4.0
caveats: Plugin install and npx install should not be combined in one project, or every workflow appears twice
Codex has no shared slash commands, so workflows are invoked as skills or by describing intent
Plugin ships no slash commands or subagents
